La TC non caratterizza i noduli tiroidei:
CT does not characterize thyroid nodules: the nature of a nodule is defined with ultrasound (TI-RADS systems: solid component, echogenicity, margins, taller-than-wide shape, microcalcifications) and with fine-needle aspiration cytology (Bethesda classification). Contrast-enhanced CT is used when the nodule is large, when retrosternal or extrathyroidal extension is suspected (trachea, esophagus, larynx, recurrent laryngeal nerve) and for the lymph node stations (level VI and lateral neck, upper mediastinum).

Practical pitfall: iodinated contrast saturates the thyroid and delays radioactive iodine therapy or scintigraphy by weeks (usually 4-8); when a differentiated carcinoma is suspected, whether it is really needed is assessed case by case.

In this case the nodule was a papillary carcinoma, follicular variant, of the right lobe: pT3 N0 M0 in AJCC 7th staging (tumor >4 cm or with minimal extrathyroidal extension). The patient was treated with surgery, radioactive iodine and hormone therapy. With AJCC 8th the age cutoff is 55 years and T3a indicates a tumor >4 cm limited to the thyroid.
